changes: p2 Hariśaṅkara: confidence lowered to medium, since the syllables 'riśa' are in brackets (supplied or uncertain in the cataloguer's reading)
p1: residence kept as written (Gautrabhūmi); the note now gives the Gauḍa identification as likely but not certain
notes: added that the last colophon calls the work 'vāsanarahasyavṛttikā', which does not match the title, and that the date checks out

notes: The author is Śaṅkara Āgamācārya, described as living in 'Gautra(bhūmi)'. This is probably a corruption of Gauḍa(bhūmi), i.e. Bengal, but that is not certain, so the residence is left as written. The syllables 'riśa' in the scribe's name are in brackets in the catalogue (supplied or unclear), so the reading Hariśaṅkara is likely but not certain. The Newari phrase 'saṃpūrṇa yāṅā juro' means 'completed (the copy)'. The final colophon names the work 'vāsanarahasyavṛttikā' instead of Tārārahasyavṛtti, probably a scribal error. The era is not stated, but the Newari wording and the karmācārya title point to Nepal Saṃvat: NS 818 = 1698 CE, which matches the catalogue.
